hints: Focus on oxidation numbers of chlorine in each reactant and product, since redox and disproportionation both depend on them.
Work out that chlorine is +5 in $\text{KClO}_3$, +7 in $\text{KClO}_4$, -1 in $\text{KCl}$, and 0 in $\text{Cl}_2$.
Remember disproportionation means the same element from one species is both oxidised and reduced, so check if chlorine alone does both jobs in equations 2 and 3.
walkthrough:
**Recall what disproportionation means**

A disproportionation is a special redox reaction where the same element in the same starting species is both oxidised (oxidation number increases) and reduced (oxidation number decreases).

Rule to use:
$$\text{same element, one reactant} \rightarrow \text{higher oxidation state + lower oxidation state}$$

**Assign oxidation numbers for chlorine**

Keep K as +1 and O as -2 to find Cl quickly.

$$\text{In KClO}_3: +1 + \text{Cl} + 3(-2) = 0 \text{ so Cl = +5}$$
$$\text{In KClO}_4: +1 + \text{Cl} + 4(-2) = 0 \text{ so Cl = +7}$$
$$\text{In KCl: Cl = -1, in Cl}_2: \text{Cl = 0}$$

**Test each equation**

Equation 1: Cl +5 to -1 (reduced) but O -2 to 0 (oxidised). This is redox, but two different elements change, so not disproportionation.

Equation 2: $4\text{KClO}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{KClO}_4 + \text{KCl}$
$$\text{Cl(+5)} \rightarrow \text{Cl(+7) oxidised and Cl(-1) reduced}$$
Same starting Cl(+5) does both, so disproportionation.

Equation 3: $6\text{KOH} + 3\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{H}_2\text{O} + 5\text{KCl} + \text{KClO}_3$
$$\text{Cl(0)} \rightarrow \text{Cl(-1) reduced and Cl(+5) oxidised}$$
Again one reactant disproportionates, so disproportionation.

**Conclude the correct statement**

Both equations 2 and 3 show chlorine being simultaneously oxidised and reduced, so both are disproportionation reactions.

options.A: Equation 1 makes $\text{O}_2$ from $\text{KClO}_3$. The chlorine-containing product is $\text{KCl}$, not chlorine $\text{Cl}_2$ or chlorate(I) $\text{ClO}^-$ which are used to kill bacteria in water treatment. This option confuses oxygen formation with chlorination.
options.B: Equation 1 is redox. Chlorine falls from +5 in $\text{KClO}_3$ to -1 in $\text{KCl}$ (reduction) while oxygen rises from -2 to 0 in $\text{O}_2$ (oxidation). Saying it is not redox ignores the oxygen change.
options.C: The product $\text{KClO}_4$ contains Cl in oxidation state +7, so it is potassium perchlorate or chlorate(VII), not chlorate(IV). The Roman numeral must match the calculated oxidation number, and +7 is not +4.
options.D: Correct. In equation 2, Cl(+5) goes to Cl(+7) and Cl(-1). In equation 3, Cl(0) goes to Cl(+5) and Cl(-1). In each case the same starting chlorine species is both oxidised and reduced, which is the definition of disproportionation.
